technical_issues.issue: Ground-track shift quoted at equator only; swath/coverage analysis ignores latitude dependence and cloud constraints on weekly revisit, though this is acknowledged as an open trade.
10 m GSD for colour-based bleaching detection from a 600 km orbit implies a demanding payload not yet addressed; acceptable at this stage.

overall: Excellent preliminary report: well-justified Australian reef-monitoring mission with quantified objectives, a robust Gantt plan with contingencies, correct hand calculations, and clear professional presentation. On track for the full assignment.

feedback.summary: An excellent preliminary report on your Great Barrier Reef coral-bleaching monitoring mission. Your quantified objectives, user-driven rationale, robust Gantt plan with contingencies, and verified orbit hand calculations all reached the Accomplished level. You are clearly on track for the full assignment; the main next steps are a top-level requirements table and addressing latitude-dependent coverage and payload demands.
next_steps: Add an explicit top-level requirements table in the Mission Concept section, tracing each requirement to an objective and user need, to close the one gap in C1.

Extend your coverage analysis beyond the 24.2° equatorial ground-track shift: quantify revisit as a function of latitude for the GBR's range and incorporate cloud-cover constraints into the weekly-revisit trade you identified.

Address the payload implications of 10 m GSD colour imaging from 600 km — begin a payload sizing trade (aperture, SNR, alternative altitude/GSD combinations) to show the imaging objective is feasible.
Complete the reference entries that lack titles and dates so all citations are fully professional.
Use your Week 10 float strategically: if the coverage trade shows one satellite cannot meet objective 1, plan time to evaluate a constellation option.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your mission goal is clear, with four quantified objectives explicitly traced to users (AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) and their needs, supported by literature [1]–[6]. To reach the very top, add an explicit top-level requirements table linking requirements to objectives and users, and begin addressing the payload demand implied by 10 m GSD from 600 km.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Your Gantt chart (Figure 1) is well structured, with Week 10 float, an explicit contingencies table with triggers and responses, and plan logic justified by the mission (orbit work before ground control because imaging requirements fix altitude and local time). Table 2 identifies information sources well. Next level: deepen contingency quantification and link each source to specific analysis tasks.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Your hand calculations are correct (a = 6978 km, T = 5801 s, i = 97.8° SSO, 24.2° track shift), STK tutorials are complete, and you interpreted results and identified the weekly-coverage trade. To strengthen further, extend the coverage analysis to latitude-dependent revisit across the GBR and include cloud constraints, not just the equatorial shift.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Your report has a logical structure, clearly labelled figures and tables (e.g., Figure 1 with a descriptive caption), consistent IEEE-style citations matching the reference list, and professional writing. Minor improvement: complete the few reference entries missing titles and dates for full consistency.
